findings.issue_text: Duplicate `downsize` method definition in app/models/optimized_image.rb:~142-151 replaces the two-argument version, breaking all existing callers that pass width and height separately (ArgumentError or malformed geometry string like "800x")
In-place downsize using ImageMagick `convert` with identical input/output paths (uploads_controller.rb:~64-66) can corrupt the file; should use `mogrify` or write to a distinct temp file
Failed downsizes are swallowed in uploads_controller.rb:~62-67: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false but the return value is ignored, so a corrupted/oversized file is passed to Upload.create_for
Client-side upload size limit hardcoded to 10MB in utilities.js:182,246 ignores per-type settings and server's actual max_image_size_kb, producing misleading 413 error messages
Downsize loop reduces dimensions geometrically (80% x 5) but file size doesn't scale linearly, so the file may still exceed the limit and upload proceeds anyway with inconsistent error reporting

Animated-GIF detection in optimized_image.rb uses extension match on tempfile path, which never matches for uploaded tempfiles, so animated GIFs are downsized with non-animated instructions and lose animation
`is_image?` check in uploads_controller.rb:~62 keys on filename which can be nil or lack an extension for API/URL-derived flows, so large images are never downsized

Blocking CPU-heavy image resize loop runs synchronously on the web request thread (uploads_controller.rb:63-68), potentially holding a Unicorn worker 10+ seconds per upload and exhausting the worker pool
Using "80%" geometry-relative downsize is the wrong tool for a file-size target; it barely reduces file size (especially for PNG), so the loop burns all 5 attempts without guaranteed convergence
The resize loop never checks whether ImageMagick succeeded, re-running on failure and wasting attempts
In-place downsize (from == to) forces ImageMagick to fully decode and re-encode in the same file, doubling I/O on the tempfile

Repeated ImageMagick execution with fixed 80% scaling is algorithmically inefficient with no feedback loop; a single-pass size-aware resize (e.g. convert -define jpeg:extent=NNNkB) would do the job in one process spawn
Animated GIF handling can explode cost when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, resizing all frames up to 5 times per upload

Hardcoded client-side 10 MB limit in utilities.js ignores the server's max_image_size_kb setting, shifting load from cheap client-side rejection to expensive server resize and incorrectly rejecting valid files for high settings
URL-download path re-downloads then resizes: API URL images exceeding max_image_size_kb now enter the synchronous resize loop, adding CPU cost per API call
downsize is defined twice in optimized_image.rb; the second definition wins, and the new 3-arg signature breaks all existing callers passing width/height, causing ArgumentError at runtime
Downsize loop in uploads_controller.rb ignores the false return value on conversion failure, so it proceeds to Upload.create_for with a still-oversized file
Up to 5 synchronous full-image ImageMagick conversions run inside the request with no timeout, creating a request-latency/DoS vector
Client max-size check hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types in utilities.js, ignoring SiteSettings limits, causing wrong 413 rejections or unhelpful errors
Image detection relies on filename from File.basename(URI.parse(url).path), so URLs without extensions bypass downsizing; should use tempfile content instead
413 error message reports hardcoded 10MB regardless of actual server limit
Downsize runs on caller-supplied tempfile in place with no error containment or integrity re-check after resizing, risking corrupted data being uploaded

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In-place downsize using ImageMagick `convert` with identical input/output paths (uploads_controller.rb:~64-66) can corrupt the file; should use `mogrify` or write to a distinct temp file

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, passing the same path for both input (`from`) and output (`to`). In `optimized_image.rb`, `downsize` ultimately builds ImageMagick instructions and executes them via `convert_with(...)` (shelling out to the command in `instructions`). Writing a `convert` output to the same filename as its input is unsafe/commonly unsupported and can fail or produce a corrupted/truncated file; the controller also ignores the return value and proceeds. This is a concrete, diff-grounded correctness/data-loss risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Failed downsizes are swallowed in uploads_controller.rb:~62-67: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false but the return value is ignored, so a corrupted/oversized file is passed to Upload.create_for

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the newly added loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but never checks its return value. In optimized_image.rb, `downsize` ultimately calls `convert_with`, which returns `false` on command failure; otherwise it does not return a truthy success value (falls through to `nil`). If the conversion fails, `tempfile.size` may remain above `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, the loop will just decrement attempts and then proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` with the still-oversized (or otherwise unprocessed) tempfile. That is a correctness issue introduced by this diff (failure is silently ignored).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side upload size limit hardcoded to 10MB in utilities.js:182,246 ignores per-type settings and server's actual max_image_size_kb, producing misleading 413 error messages
Downsize loop reduces dimensions geometrically (80% x 5) but file size doesn't scale linearly, so the file may still exceed the limit and upload proceeds anyway with inconsistent error reporting

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop downsizes the image up to 5 times (`attempt = 5` … `while ... tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` then `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)`) but does not check/handle the case where the file is still above `max_image_size_kb` after the loop. The code then proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` regardless. Whether that ultimately rejects the upload is not shown in the diff, but the newly added logic is incomplete for this edge case and could lead to confusing behavior/error reporting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Animated-GIF detection in optimized_image.rb uses extension match on tempfile path, which never matches for uploaded tempfiles, so animated GIFs are downsized with non-animated instructions and lose animation

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new “auto-reduce” loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`. In optimized_image.rb, `optimize` decides whether to use `*_instructions_animated` via `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Here `from` is the tempfile path, which typically has no `.gif` extension, so the animated branch won’t be selected even for an uploaded animated GIF. That makes it likely animated GIFs will be processed with non-animated instructions and lose animation, a behavior introduced/exposed by this diff’s new downsizing of uploaded images.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `is_image?` check in uploads_controller.rb:~62 keys on filename which can be nil or lack an extension for API/URL-derived flows, so large images are never downsized

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb#create_upload`, the new downsizing block is gated by `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`. In the API/URL path, `filename` is derived from `File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)`, which can be empty or lack an extension (e.g., URLs ending with `/image`), causing `is_image?` (which appears to key off the name) to return false and skip downsizing even if the downloaded file is actually an image. That defeats the stated intent of allowing large images to be uploaded and reduced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blocking CPU-heavy image resize loop runs synchronously on the web request thread (uploads_controller.rb:63-68), potentially holding a Unicorn worker 10+ seconds per upload and exhausting the worker pool

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a synchronous loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that may run up to 5 iterations, calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` each time (which ultimately shells out via backticks in `convert_with`). This work happens inline on the web request thread before `Upload.create_for`, so it can block a Unicorn worker while CPU/IO-heavy image processing runs. The exact “10+ seconds” duration isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the synchronous, potentially expensive behavior is clearly introduced here and is a legitimate scalability concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Using "80%" geometry-relative downsize is the wrong tool for a file-size target; it barely reduces file size (especially for PNG), so the loop burns all 5 attempts without guaranteed convergence

adjudication.rationale: The new server-side loop in `uploads_controller.rb` tries to hit a **file-size** threshold by repeatedly calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%")` up to 5 times while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. The diff shows no guarantee this converges to the byte-size limit within 5 iterations (it’s a fixed geometric scale, not a size-targeted recompress), and there’s no fallback behavior if the file remains oversized—so the loop may do work without achieving its intended goal. The specific claim about PNGs “barely” shrinking is plausible but not directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The resize loop never checks whether ImageMagick succeeded, re-running on failure and wasting attempts

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop retries downsizing up to 5 times based only on `tempfile.size` (`while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > ...`), but it ignores the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)`. In `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` returns `false` on ImageMagick failure, and `optimize`/`downsize` would propagate that, yet the controller never checks it. If ImageMagick fails (e.g., corrupt image), the loop will still decrement attempts and re-run, wasting attempts and potentially proceeding with an oversized file afterward.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In-place downsize (from == to) forces ImageMagick to fully decode and re-encode in the same file, doubling I/O on the tempfile

adjudication.rationale: The diff newly introduces in-place image processing: in `uploads_controller.rb`, `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` uses the same path for `from` and `to`. That can create unnecessary read+write work (and may be suboptimal compared to writing to a separate temp output then swapping). However, the claim about ImageMagick behavior and I/O doubling isn’t directly verifiable from the diff because the exact command generated in `*_instructions` isn’t shown here, so this is best treated as a concrete performance/implementation concern rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Repeated ImageMagick execution with fixed 80% scaling is algorithmically inefficient with no feedback loop; a single-pass size-aware resize (e.g. convert -define jpeg:extent=NNNkB) would do the job in one process spawn

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds a loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that can invoke `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to 5 times while the file is still above `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`:
```rb
attempt = 5
while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes
  OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)
  attempt -= 1
end
```
Each iteration spawns an ImageMagick/convert process (via `OptimizedImage.convert_with` backticks), and it always uses the same "80%" scaling factor rather than adjusting based on how far over the size limit the image is. This is an efficiency/architecture concern (extra process spawns, potentially unnecessary work) but not a verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Animated GIF handling can explode cost when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, resizing all frames up to 5 times per upload

adjudication.rationale: The new upload logic in `uploads_controller.rb` adds a loop that can run up to 5 times: `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. In `optimized_image.rb`, when `allow_animation` is true and the source matches `\.GIF$`, it switches to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which typically implies processing all frames. This creates a real performance/cost concern for large animated GIF uploads because the potentially expensive animated resize can repeat multiple times per upload. The diff doesn’t show functional incorrectness, but it does introduce a concrete resource-usage risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded client-side 10 MB limit in utilities.js ignores the server's max_image_size_kb setting, shifting load from cheap client-side rejection to expensive server resize and incorrectly rejecting valid files for high settings

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` in `utilities.js` both for the pre-upload size check and the 413 handling, replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. This will incorrectly reject uploads >10MB even when server settings allow larger sizes, and can also allow uploads up to 10MB when server settings are smaller (pushing work to the server-side path, which now includes a resize loop in `uploads_controller.rb`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: URL-download path re-downloads then resizes: API URL images exceeding max_image_size_kb now enter the synchronous resize loop, adding CPU cost per API call

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the API URL path now downloads up to a fixed `10.megabytes` (instead of `max_image_size_kb`) and then immediately enters a synchronous loop that repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` (up to 5 attempts). That adds CPU/work to each API upload request for oversized images. However, the diff does not show any re-download happening—only a single download followed by resizing—so the “re-downloads” part is inaccurate, but the synchronous resize-cost concern is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: downsize is defined twice in optimized_image.rb; the second definition wins, and the new 3-arg signature breaks all existing callers passing width/height, causing ArgumentError at runtime

adjudication.rationale: In optimized_image.rb, `self.downsize` is indeed defined twice: first as `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, then later redefined as `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby, the second definition replaces the first (no overloading). Any existing callers still passing `max_width, max_height` (e.g. 4 positional args) will now bind `dimensions=max_width` and `opts=max_height` (an Integer), causing failures when `optimize` treats `opts` like a Hash (e.g. `opts[:allow_animation]`), and callers passing 5 args (with an options hash) would raise ArgumentError. This defect is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsize loop in uploads_controller.rb ignores the false return value on conversion failure, so it proceeds to Upload.create_for with a still-oversized file

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but never checks its return value. `OptimizedImage.optimize` calls `convert_with(...)`, which returns `false` on conversion failure; the controller ignores this and only decrements `attempt`. After 5 failed conversions, it will still proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` even if `tempfile.size` remains above `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Image detection relies on filename from File.basename(URI.parse(url).path), so URLs without extensions bypass downsizing; should use tempfile content instead

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new downsizing block gates on `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` where `filename` for URL uploads is derived from `File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)`. If the URL path lacks an extension or a meaningful basename, `is_image?` may not recognize it as an image and the downsizing loop will be skipped, undermining the stated goal of auto-reducing oversized images. The diff doesn’t show how `is_image?` works, so the bypass is plausible but not fully verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 413 error message reports hardcoded 10MB regardless of actual server limit

adjudication.rationale: In the 413 handler in `utilities.js`, `maxSizeKB` is hardcoded to `10 * 1024` (10MB) instead of using a setting like `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` (which it previously did). This means the "file too large" alert will always report 10MB even if the actual server/upload limit differs, so the error message can be incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsize runs on caller-supplied tempfile in place with no error containment or integrity re-check after resizing, risking corrupted data being uploaded

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `uploads_controller.rb` repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` (same input/output path) and ignores any return value or failure signal. There’s no rescue/rollback or integrity check after conversion before proceeding to `Upload.create_for(...)`, so a failed/partial in-place convert could leave a corrupted or unexpected file being uploaded. The diff doesn’t prove corruption will occur, but the lack of error handling around an in-place transformation is a concrete robustness issue introduced here.
